Online marketplace Etsy has announced plans to eliminate approximately 220 jobs, representing 12% of its global workforce, as part of a sweeping organisational restructuring under Chief Executive Officer Kruti Patel Goyal. The reduction will bring the company's total headcount down to roughly 1,600 employees, with the majority of the affected positions concentrated within the product, engineering, design, research, and analytics departments.

The announcement coincided with the release of Etsy's second-quarter financial results, which demonstrated stable underlying momentum despite broader pressures in discretionary retail spending. Quarterly revenue rose by 6.2% year on year to reach 668.3 million USD, outperforming analyst expectations, while marketplace gross merchandise sales saw positive growth.

As per a Analytics Insight report, the strategic shift is intended to simplify internal processes, improve inter-departmental collaboration, and accelerate product development rather than serve as a direct cost-reduction exercise. Leadership noted that the company's historical growth had introduced overlapping responsibilities and management layers, which the latest changes aim to eliminate by creating smaller, more agile teams.
